title: Never push a branch whose tests fail
summary: pre-push runs after you type push and before anything leaves your machine. Use it for the checks that are too slow for pre-commit — a test run, a lint pass, a WIP guard.
mental_model: `pre-push` gets the remote name and URL as arguments, and one `<local-ref> <local-sha> <remote-ref> <remote-sha>` line per ref on stdin. It is the last cheap moment to catch a mistake before other people see it.

write.content:
#!/bin/sh
python -c "import calc; assert calc.total([1,2,3]) == 6; print('tests passed')"

steps.title: Install the hook
steps.why: It reads the refs being pushed from stdin, refuses anything whose commits look like work in progress, and runs the test suite once. Slow checks belong here rather than in pre-commit, because you push far less often than you commit.

write.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Block WIP commits and failing tests from leaving this machine.

remote="$1"
ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
status=0

while read local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  [ "$local_sha" = "$ZERO" ] && continue   # deletion, nothing to check

  if [ "$remote_sha" = "$ZERO" ]; then
    range="$local_sha"
  else
    range="$remote_sha..$local_sha"
  fi

  if git log --format=%s $range | grep -qiE '^(wip|fixup!|squash!|temp|do not push)'; then
    echo "pre-push: $local_ref contains work-in-progress commits" >&2
    git log --oneline $range | head -5 >&2
    status=1
  fi
done

if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "pre-push: running tests..." >&2
  if ! sh run_tests.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "pre-push: tests failed, refusing to push to $remote" >&2
    sh run_tests.sh >&2
    status=1
  fi
fi

exit $status

steps.expect: The tests pass right now, so the hook would allow a push.

steps.title: Break the code and try to push
steps.why: The commit itself succeeds — pre-commit has no opinion about tests. The push is where it is caught, which is exactly the right boundary: your local history can be messy, what you publish should not be broken.
steps.expect: The commit exists locally; the push is refused with the test output.

verify.label: the broken code never reached the server
…but the commit is still safely on your machine

steps.title: Fix it and push
steps.why: With the tests passing the hook exits zero and git proceeds as normal. The hook is invisible when everything is fine, which is what makes it tolerable.

steps.title: Now the WIP guard
steps.why: A commit titled 'wip' is a note to yourself, not something a reviewer should see. The hook scans only the commits actually being pushed, using the remote sha git hands it on stdin.
steps.expect: Refused, with the offending commits listed.

verify.label: the WIP branch was not published

steps.title: Tidy the history, then push
steps.why: Amend into a real message and the same push succeeds. The hook has nudged you into the habit of publishing readable history without anyone having to review it first.

actions.run: git commit -q --amend -m "Add calibrated dosing with validation"

verify.label: the tidied branch published fine
verify.hint: amend the wip message to something real

steps.title: Know the escape hatch and its cost
steps.why: `--no-verify` skips it. Legitimate when you need to publish a branch for a colleague to look at mid-debugging — and a reason the same checks belong in CI as well.
steps.expect: Nothing to run; the point is knowing the flag exists.

verify.label: only passing code reached the server
verify.hint: the hook must exit non-zero when run_tests.sh fails

verify.label: the feature branch published once its message was tidied

pitfalls: pre-push runs once for the whole push but gets a line per ref. Pushing several branches at once means checking all of them.
A hook that takes thirty seconds trains people to use `--no-verify`. Keep it to the fast tests and leave the rest to CI.
The hook runs in the repository root regardless of where you typed the command, so relative paths in it are safe.
`$remote_sha` is all zeroes for a brand-new branch. Handle that case, or your range expression is invalid and the hook errors on first push.
cheatsheet: one line per ref, on stdin
the branch is new on the remote
